designer-initial.summary: Selected a bounded observation acquisition and radio-delivery coordinator with an exact 8/21/20/8 medium-tier specification and complete ownership, priority, recovery, retry, and finite-partition audits.
questions_for_model: Can the eight semantic usages and 21 interactions be realized flat at depth one, or do the trusted SysML-AADL forms require the predeclared single behavior-free support container and 12 uncredited delegations?

Can SessionSnapshot and OperatorCoordinationStatus use GUMBO-inspectable finite fields without conflating repeated classifiers or moving advisory logic into a routing usage, and what uncredited field projections are required?

Can the retained analyzer independently compose all eight owner relations over 4,320 end-to-end valuations and separately check all 3,675 structurally valid outcome-policy inputs, including producer-unreachable combinations?

model-review.summary: The 8/21/20/8 allocation is realizable unchanged using the authorized single support Process, and all eight owners are behaviorally substantive.

findings.evidence: Trusted and retained accepted sources use System-to-Process-to-Thread containment for contract-bearing Threads. A fresh harness-equivalent Sireum typecheck of the retained factory material-continuity source exited 0 with Well-formed!. For this design, the 12 boundary semantic INTs are each realized once inside the Process plus one transparent root/Process delegation, while the nine internal INTs remain direct: 12*2+9 gives exactly 33 raw declarations, nine non-root nodes, depth two, and the unchanged 21 semantic interactions.

The trusted/accepted forms demonstrate GUMBO contracts local to Threads, Data-record field access through attribute members, and publication of pre-evaluation state with In(local_state) while the same owner commits post-evaluation state. Thus INT-14, SessionSnapshot, OperatorCoordinationStatus, the sole PART-07 state owner, and PART-08-local advisory/notice derivation require no absent input, shadow state, or routing owner.

Extensional audit: PART-01 is a 4-to-3 invalidity-precedence classification; PART-02 is a 6-to-4 assessment/context classification; PART-03 and PART-04 are each 6-to-4 unavailability-precedence classifications; PART-05 is a 320-input phase/precedence proposal relation; PART-06 is a 48-input intent/proposal priority relation; PART-07 is an 85-input state-dependent transition and output-tuple relation; and PART-08 is a 3,675-input advisory/notice classification. Copied fields, command encodings, and any representation-only enum projection are explicitly uncredited, so no claimed owner is a one-to-one rename, copy, bundle, or reroute wrapper.

The retained analyzer can separately enumerate all eight local products, compose their transmitted values over all 4,320 end-to-end valuations, compare them with an independently structured raw-input reference relation, retain reachable versus structurally valid unreachable results, execute all eight state-carrying scenario families, and bind its report to the canonical source hash. Current harness behavior fails nonzero analyzer exit, source-hash mismatch, failed ownership records, or nonzero gaps, overlaps, and mismatches.

designer-resolution.summary: Approved unchanged semantics with the preauthorized 9-node, 33-declaration support-Process realization selected for generation.

model-generation.summary: Removed the unsupported qualification-role ownership claim from the campaign-v1 audit without changing source semantics; reran SysML typechecking and the bounded analyzer, then confirmed source hashes, medium counts, metrics, analyzer evidence, and traceability are mutually consistent.

visualization.summary: Accepted one validated, trace-audited system overview with eight semantic responsibilities inside generated-support containment, 23 representative routed edges, and zero crossings or route-object collisions.

designer-final.summary: Source, bounded semantics, ownership integrity, traceability, and rendered overview passed; executable evidence was not required.
